b: Since the latest and greatest new trolling motors are now designed for either 24- or 36-volt batteries, a 24-volt battery is becoming a bit of an enigma in new bass boats of today.

If we were to get a new 36-volt trolling motor, the batteries could be upgraded then. But it’s not imperative since the new brushless designs are super-efficient with the 24-volt option. Both run equally well at full charge. And if you run a 36-volt trolling motor, your best option may just be the MillerTech 36V 105AH and its longer run time.

However, if you are running a trolling motor specifically designed for 24 volts, the MillerTech 24 volt 80 AH Lithium Battery has proven to deliver six to eight hours of reliable power. And it’s also an excellent choice to run in parallel with a second battery, which can maximize your run time to more than 12 hours.
Let’s take a look at it.

The lithium cells are UL-, CE-, RoHS-, and RU-approved. They come equipped with stainless steel breather vents, which allow for the air flow that prevents condensation on top of the case. The marine batteries are also sealed with a rubber gasket to insure no water gets inside.

A single 24-volt battery is a great option to save space, too. And combined with the 24-volt, 15-amp charger, this setup is a solid one. Because we had a 24-volt trolling motor and ample sump space, we tested two 24-volt batteries combined with the waterproof charger together. We have an older 24 volt Minn Kota Fortrex that still had plenty of life and was in good shape, so it was the best option for us without breaking the bank on upgrades.
A 24 volt battery needs a 24 volt charger, like this one from MillerTech.
Something that’s a battery must-have for the seasoned angler is a Bluetooth package. And the MillerTech version is second to none — which is a huge criteria with our selection.

Designed for iOS or Android, the MillerTech app gives users real-time data. That information includes remaining capacity, voltage, current, and temperature, and works on up to six batteries in the same app.

With the built-in battery management system (BMS), the user can prevent overcharge, over-discharge, internal over-temperature, voltage issues, and short-circuiting. It also provides cell protection, too. The low-voltage alarm also notifies the user when voltage gets too low. They’re all great protection attributes typical of the MillerTech lineup.

The quandary is that, honestly, there is not much difference in price between a 24- and a 36-volt battery, so many boaters are opting to go with the 36. It truly depends on the year and make of the trolling motor for the best selection. But with the 24V 80AH Lithium Battery being another fine example of MillerTech’s product line, it’s definitely a solid investment at $1,099.
While the 24V 80AH Sport Series Lithium Battery with Bluetooth is presently out of stock on MillerTech’s website, you can find it at other online retailers.
